points.t: Plaque, scalp or flexural psoriasis needing more than a steroid, or a patient referred for **light treatment**.
Vitamin D analogues normalise keratinocyte growth; tar and dithranol slow proliferation; UVB and PUVA suppress skin immune cells.
**Potent steroid + vitamin D** (separately or combined) first; **calcitriol** for face / flexures; phototherapy is specialist.
**Hypercalcaemia** with excess vitamin D analogue; burns and skin cancer with cumulative **PUVA**.

cause.lead: Different ways to slow the plaque.
points: **Vitamin D analogues** bind the VDR: slow keratinocyte proliferation, normalise differentiation, lower IL-17 / IL-8. Flatten and de-scale more than they de-redden.
**Coal tar** activates the aryl hydrocarbon receptor: normalises differentiation, restores filaggrin; antipruritic; phototoxic with UVA.
**Dithranol** makes free radicals: anti-proliferative; stains and burns normal skin.
**UV** suppresses skin immune cells: NB-UVB stays superficial, UVA reaches deeper.

visuals.caption: Light depth in skin: narrowband UVB (311–313 nm) acts mainly in the epidermis; UVA (320–400 nm, used with psoralen in PUVA) reaches the dermis.
visuals.alt: Skin section with a short UVB beam and a deeper UVA beam

features.lead: Know the products and where each fits.
points: **Calcipotriol** 50 micrograms/g ointment or scalp solution; with betamethasone dipropionate 0.05% as gel, ointment or foam.
**Calcitriol** 3 micrograms/g: gentler, face and flexures. **Tacalcitol** 4 micrograms/g: once daily.
**Coal tar**: creams, ointments, shampoos; crude tar in specialist units.
**Dithranol**: short-contact for chronic plaques in specialist / day units.
**NB-UVB** first-line phototherapy; **PUVA** for thick or resistant psoriasis, PPP, hand eczema, mycosis fungoides.

visuals.caption: Narrowband UVB is delivered in a hospital cabinet with UV goggles. Dose, course length and lifetime total are recorded like a drug.
visuals.alt: Patient in a phototherapy cabinet with a nurse

points: Potent TCS od + vitamin D od, separately, **up to 4 weeks**.
No better at **8 weeks**: vitamin D bd alone.
Still poor at 8–12 weeks: potent TCS bd ≤ 4 weeks, coal tar, or combined product.
Calcipotriol **100 g / week**.
Combination: **15 g / day, 100 g / week, ≤ 30% BSA**, 4-week courses.
Calcitriol **30 g / day**, ≤ 35% BSA.
Hypercalcaemia, severe renal impairment; caution in erythrodermic or pustular psoriasis.

cards.name: Potent steroid alone
cards.clue: Faster on redness; atrophy and rebound with long use.

cards.name: Combined calcipotriol + betamethasone
cards.clue: One daily application; **contains a steroid**: count it.

cards.name: Coal tar
cards.clue: Messy, odour, stains; very low cancer risk at therapeutic doses.

manage.lead: Topicals in primary care; light is specialist-delivered.

points: Wash hands after; keep calcipotriol **off the face**; irritation usually settles.
With phototherapy, apply vitamin D **after** UV, not before.
**Steroid in the morning, vitamin D at night** (or the reverse) for up to 4 weeks, or one combined product daily.
Vitamin D bd; coal tar; combined product; calcitriol for face and flexures.
NB-UVB (often safest step-up in **pregnancy**), PUVA, dithranol, systemics.

limits.t: Over weekly maximum or symptoms: check calcium, stop.
UVA-blocking eye protection ~24 h after oral psoralen; lifelong skin checks.
Avoid inflamed / pustular skin, face, genitals; avoid sun after (phototoxic).

items.t: Erythrodermic or generalised pustular psoriasis: urgent dermatology.
Not controlled on topicals at 8–12 weeks: refer for phototherapy or systemics.

pearls.t: ‘Steroid in the morning, vitamin D at night’.
Combined products are steroids: use breaks.
Tar shampoo: lather, leave 5–10 minutes, rinse; may discolour light or dyed hair.

quiz.q: NICE first-line topical for trunk plaque psoriasis?
quiz.a: Potent steroid once daily + vitamin D analogue once daily, applied separately, up to 4 weeks.

quiz.q: Which vitamin D analogue for face and flexures?
Advice after oral psoralen for PUVA?
quiz.a: UVA-blocking eye protection for about 24 hours.
